facts.fact: According to a third-party adoption figure cited by Adwave (electroiq.com), 87.6% of websites were using a valid SSL certificate by 2024.
facts.quote: By 2024, 87.6% of websites were using a valid SSL certificate, up from 18.5% six years earlier

facts.fact: According to the same third-party adoption figure cited by Adwave, 18.5% of websites were using a valid SSL certificate six years before 2024.
Adwave's guide describes the SSL digital handshake between browser and server as having five steps.
facts.quote: An infographic showing the five steps of the SSL digital handshake process for secure website connection.

facts.fact: A UCC certificate can cover up to 100 domains, according to the Adwave page, which cites an external guide for certificate scope.
facts.quote: A **UCC** certificate can cover **up to 100 domains**, which can simplify management for businesses handling multiple sites

facts.fact: A single-domain SSL certificate secures one hostname.
A wildcard SSL certificate covers one domain and all of its subdomains.
facts.quote: A **wildcard** certificate covers one domain and all its subdomains.

facts.fact: Adwave's checklist recommends five checks to run this week to catch most SSL issues.
facts.quote: ### Five checks to run this week

facts.fact: According to the Adwave page, SSL only protects data in transit and does not protect against phishing, server malware, weak passwords, or vulnerable plugins.
facts.quote: It only protects data **in transit**. It doesn't stop phishing, server malware, weak passwords, or vulnerable plugins.

facts.fact: The Adwave page says a page can lose the padlock when some images, scripts, or forms still call for HTTP resources, a problem known as mixed content.
facts.quote: A page can load over HTTPS and still break the padlock if some parts of it, like images, scripts, or forms, still call for HTTP resources.
